correctness.rationale: The centered edge-difference Minkowski sum has x_i=t_i-t_{i-1}, |t_i|<=1/2. Feasibility of cyclic differences is exactly that partial-sum range <=1, equivalent to all proper cyclic-interval inequalities |sum_I x_i|<=1. The intrinsic normal of a length-s interval has squared norm s(n-s)/n and gives the displayed inradius and all ball-center inequalities. Odd n=2k+1: all k-block equalities imply c_i=c_{i+k}; gcd(k,2k+1)=1 gives c=0. Even n=2k: all k-block equalities force c_i=c_{i+k} and zero half-sum, while near-balanced lengths k±1 force |y_i|<=beta_k. Any other block length k±j has center sum bounded by j beta; convex f(j)=1-sqrt(1-j^2/k^2) >= j f(1) establishes sufficiency. Exact cube-hyperplane vertices have >=k-1 coordinate endpoints, yielding parity-dependent closed counts. Independently all 5,880 stated even-cycle interval inequalities were tested for candidate vertices n<=12. Analytical proof, not the finite test, covers all n.

final_claim: For centered unit-edge graphical zonotope of C_n in H_n (n>=3), intrinsic Euclidean inradius rho=sqrt(n/floor(n^2/4)). All max-radius centers: odd n => {0}; even n=2k => {(y,y):sum_{i=1}^k y_i=0, |y_i|<=1-sqrt(1-k^-2)}. Its dimension k-1 and vertices binom(k,k/2) for even k or k binom(k-1,(k-1)/2) for odd k.
limitations: Intrinsic Euclidean metric in H_n, n>=3, unit-weight edge segments with half-length 1/2; graph C_n not general unicyclic or weighted; even center dimension is k-1, not ambient n-1.
